IF YOU WANT TO BECOME A TOP 1% BACKEND ENGINEER, STOP ADDING MICROSERVICES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 RULES: 1/5

Start with a monolith until it hurts.

One deploy, one database, one log stream. Split only when a team or scale boundary forces you. 2/5

Every network call is a failure waiting.

Timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers. Assume every dependency will die at 3am. 3/5

Make slow things async.

Emails, webhooks, reports. If the user doesn't need it now, queue it and return fast. 4/5

I post daily breakdowns like this for backend, SQL, and interviews.

Follow @owlsky17 so you don't miss the next one. 5/5

IF YOU WANT APIS THAT DON'T BREAK CLIENTS, STOP GUESSING STATUS CODES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 RULES: 1/5

200 means done, 201 means created.

Return the resource location with 201. Clients should never guess where their object went. 2/5

400 is their fault, 500 is yours.

Validation errors get 400 with field-level messages. Never leak a stack trace with a 500. 3/5

Version in the URL, paginate every list.

/v1 today saves you tomorrow. Limit plus cursor beats offset for anything that grows. 4/5

IF YOU WANT SYSTEMS THAT SURVIVE TRAFFIC SPIKES, STOP HOPING.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 DEFENSES: 1/5

Cache the hot path first.

Profile before optimizing. One cached query at the top endpoint beats ten micro-tweaks elsewhere. 2/5

Rate limit everything public.

Per key, per IP, per user. The cheapest outage to prevent is the one an abuser causes. 3/5

Load test before launch, not after.

2x expected traffic in staging. Finding the bottleneck at midnight is a choice. 4/5
